subject: zoology
question_text: 'Entamoeba histolytica is an obligatory anaerobe'. Justify.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.59, VSAQ 144). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Where it lives
lines: Entamoeba histolytica lives in the large
Free oxygen is not available there, and the
parasite has no mitochondria in its body.
steps.why: Two facts have to sit side by side — no oxygen outside the parasite and no mitochondria inside it — because together they leave the parasite no way to use oxygen at all.
common_mistakes: Writing that it lives in the small intestine. It lives in the large intestine.
Leaving out the mitochondria. The absence of mitochondria is half the reason.
steps.memory_tip: No oxygen around it and no mitochondria in it: both halves are needed.
steps.margin_note: Two lines. Name the habitat and the missing organelle.

steps.label: Justification

lines.text: No oxygen, no mitochondria: anaerobic only

lines: It gets its energy without using oxygen.
It can live only in the absence of oxygen, so it
steps.why: 'Obligatory' means there is no alternative, so the closing sentence must say the parasite can live ONLY without oxygen, not merely that it does live without oxygen.
common_mistakes: Writing that it can live with or without oxygen. That would be a facultative anaerobe.
Ending without using the words obligatory anaerobe.
steps.memory_tip: Obligatory means no choice: it cannot use oxygen at all.
steps.margin_note: Two short lines ending in the term the question quotes.

insider_note: The word 'obligatory' is what is being tested — say the parasite can live ONLY without oxygen, not just that it does.
